chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan 'an Zur'ah 'an Sama'ah said:

I asked him about the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for one who intends to fast, so he said: 'As for Ramadan, then indeed there is merit in the suhur, even with a sip of water. As for voluntary fasting outside of Ramadan, then whoever wishes to take the pre-dawn meal, let him do so, and whoever does not do so, there is no harm.'

key_terms.السَّحُور: The pre-dawn meal eaten before fasting begins

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and merit of eating the pre-dawn meal (suhur) during Ramadan versus voluntary fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the distinction between the obligatory Ramadan fast and voluntary (nafl) fasting, emphasizing that while suhur is a highly meritorious Sunnah in Ramadan—even with just a sip of water—it remains recommended but not strictly required for voluntary fasts. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the spiritual benefits of suhur extend beyond Ramadan, encouraging consistency in prophetic traditions regardless of the fasting context.
